newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain to contribute 500 troops to Albania force.
newsitem.headline: Spain to contribute 500 troops to Albania force.

text.p: Spain will contribute 500 peacekeepers to an Italian-led multinational security force for Albania to protect humanitarian relief operations in the country, the defence ministry said on Monday.
"Spain will send about 500 soldiers," a defence ministry spokeswoman said. No date has been set yet for the Spanish contingent's departure.
Defence Minister Eduardo Serra said earlier the force will face risks but is unlikely to be engaged in armed clashes.
"It will be a force which will not be confronted with armed actions," Serra said in a television interview.

The 5,000-strong force is being put together after receiving approval from the United Nations on Friday. Among countries expected to contribute are Italy, France, Greece, Spain, Portugal, Romania and Turkey.
Serra said Italy is expected to contribute 2,000 to 2,500 troops.
About half of the force will be deployed initially and the rest will be in reserve. The first men are expected to arrive in Albania in the next few weeks.
Albania's parliament, dominated by President Sali Berisha's Democratic Party, voted on Sunday to accept the multinational force.
